page: Microsoft Azure E128-32ds_v6 is an Edsv6-family virtual machine configured with 32 dedicated vCPUs and 1024.0 GB of RAM. Powered by an Intel Xeon 8573C processor with an x86_64 architecture, it features 16 physical cores, 2 threads per core, and a clock speed of 4.2 GHz. The processor includes a 260 MB L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX). This instance is equipped with 7559 GB of local storage and is Premium Storage capable, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor.

Benchmark data shows strong memory performance, with large-block read-only memory bandwidth reaching 238.84 GB/sec and write bandwidth at 137.13 GB/sec, both placing in the top 25%. Single-threaded gzip compression is also strong at 31.18 GB/sec. In CPU-bound tasks, the server achieves an average stress-ng multi-core score of 31881.31 and a PassMark CPU score of 47316.29, with a strong physics test score of 7302.83. For database and web operations, it delivers an average of 43.41 million Redis SET operations per second and a strong static web serving throughput of 44.43 GB/sec. LLM inference benchmarks using a 135M model show strong prompt processing at 2558.78 tokens/sec and text generation at 317.03 tokens/sec.

From a resource density perspective, the E128-32ds_v6 offers an exceptionally high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 32 GB per vCPU, paired with massive local storage. This profile provides high qualitative cost efficiency for memory-bound and storage-intensive workloads that do not require a proportional scaling of compute cores. However, the tradeoff is that CPU-bound benchmarks, such as stress-ng and PassMark CPU scores, fall within the average tier, indicating that workloads requiring raw compute scaling rather than memory capacity may find less value in this configuration.

This server is configured for memory-intensive and storage-heavy workloads. Appropriate use cases include large-scale relational databases, in-memory caching systems like Redis, data warehousing, enterprise resource planning (ERP) systems, and memory-bound data analytics.
